diffs.diff: log10(illuminance in lux): datasheet reading gives 1.5152 per count, the part's model has 1.471
diffs.evidence: Sharp GA1A1S202WP spec sheet section 3.3, note *2: 'Sensor output vs. illuminance is logarithmic. Io=10 x log(Ev) (uA)' (typ 20 uA at 100 lx, 30 uA at 1000 lx). Adafruit #1384 product page: 'On this breakout we placed a 68K ohm resistor from OUT to ground to turn the current into a voltage'. So V = 10 uA x 68 kOhm x log10(lux) = 0.68 V/decade, i.e. log10(lux) = V / 0.68 = 1.4706 x V, which is the model's 1.471. The second reading's 1.5152 = 5.0/3.3 comes from Adafruit's simplified example sketch on the learn guide ('float logRange = 5.0; // 3.3v = 10^5 lux'), a rough end-point approximation rather than the datasheet transfer function (at 1000 lx it would give 1.98 V vs the datasheet's 30 uA x 68k = 2.04 V).
